Done. The T3 export completed on the first execution and the self-report is written.

**What the script does** (`out/T3/solution.py`):
- Loads the 244 input tensors and classifies them with anchored regexes: one for the 4 projection matrices per layer, one for the 3 buffers per layer. Counts are checked against 64 and 48 before any casting.
- Casts the projection matrices to bfloat16 and everything else to float32, dropping the buffers. Key order is preserved.
- Runs the required checks plus extras: 64 bfloat16 tensors, layer 0 query_key_value is bfloat16, embed_in is float32, 196 tensors total, every tensor is either bfloat16 or float32, no shape changed.
- Packs shards greedily in key order with a 256 MiB budget, placing any oversized tensor alone. Refuses to overwrite existing output, writes HF-style shard names and an index with weight_map and total_size, then re-reads every shard to confirm dtypes, shapes and index consistency.

**Result:**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Executions | 1, no failures |
| Shards | 9 |
| Tensors written | 196 |
| Embedding shards | embed_in and embed_out alone, one per shard |
| Largest mixed shard | 260,317,184 bytes, under the 268,435,456 budget |

**One note for the report:** the task quotes the embeddings at 206 MB, which is their float16 size. After the mandated float32 upcast they are 412 MB each, still over budget, so the standalone-shard rule applies as expected. The packing strategy and shard naming were unspecified, so I used the HuggingFace convention and recorded that in `out/T3/REPORT.md`.
